sections.h2: Who sends Henry County tax bills
sections.html:
Henry County runs its own billing through the Tax Commissioner, with a separate Board of Assessors deciding what each parcel is worth. The commissioner receives the money for the county, schools and other levying bodies and hands it on. Billing questions and value questions land at different desks, so choose before you dial.

Henry County tax contacts by task
TaskWherePhone
Pay, file homestead, ask about a lienTax Commissioner, 140 Henry Parkway, McDonough, GA 30253(770) 288-8180
Same tasks in the north endTax Commissioner, 164 Burke Street, Stockbridge, GA 30281(770) 288-8180
Value questions and mailing address changesTax Assessors, 140 Henry Parkway, McDonough(770) 288-7999, option 1
Pay with an automated lineNeeds tax year plus bill number1-855-255-6196

Drop boxes sit at both commissioner offices. For mailed checks, make them payable to Henry County Tax Commissioner or HCTC, send them to 140 Henry Pkwy, and write the bill numbers on the check. Metered mail does not count as proof of timely mailing.

McDonough is the county seat, joined by Stockbridge, Hampton and Locust Grove. The county has 264,922 residents as of July 2025 on 318.71 square miles of land, and 1,666 building permits were issued in 2025, so unsold new homes and resales share the market.

  • Typical owner-occupied home: $313,900 (2020 to 2024 median).
  • Homeowners hold 74.9% of occupied housing.
  • Rent at the median: $1,674 per month.
  • Median household income: $83,146.

At those values, a small error in the square footage on file moves the bill, so check your digest record before setting a price.

Statements go to the January 1 owner and are payable on or before November 16, with mailing by mid-September. Counties may move the statewide December 20 default earlier, which is what this date reflects. Whatever the calendar says, follow the date on the bill you receive.

Late payment gets costly. Interest builds monthly and a further 5% penalty attaches every 120 days after the deadline, up to a ceiling of 20%. Mailed checks need a USPS postmark before the deadline. Since December 2025 the county reads that mark as the first automated processing date at a regional center, which can be later than the day you dropped the envelope off. A transfer from your bank's own bill-pay service has no postmark, so the money must be in hand by the deadline.

  • The online portal charges 2.5% on cards or $1.50 for an e-check, a fee set by its outside processor.
  • Daily ceilings are $20,000 on cards and $60,000 on e-checks.
  • Paying at a counter does not waive the card fee.
  • If a lender escrows your tax, the lender is the contact for the bill.

sections.h2: Will Henry County bill the buyer after closing?
sections.html:
Not automatically. Statements go to the person who owned on January 1, and a lien is filed against that owner unless the office receives a settlement statement inside 90 days of the due date, under Georgia Code 48-3-3. Send page one, where county taxes appear as collected, to propertytax@henrycountyga.gov with the address or a copy of the bill.

The owner on January 1 is responsible for the entire year with no partial refund. Look at the Henry County line on your closing statement before signing, and as the seller, send the paper yourself instead of assuming someone else did.

Other charges can share the bill. Streetlight, stormwater and sanitation fees appear on it, and a county water charge called the 2 mill tax pays for storage and pipes whether or not a home has a well. The Water Authority at 770-957-6659 explains that line.

  1. Get the settlement statement from the closing agent on closing day.
  2. Email page one to the address above, with the parcel address.
  3. Keep the sent message for your records in case the office asks for it later.

File in person at either commissioner office, through the online option, or by mail postmarked on or before April 1, since only a USPS postmark counts. One filing covers you for as long as you stay put. Bring these items.

  • Driver's licenses for you and your spouse that show the property address.
  • Registrations for every vehicle at that address.
  • The warranty deed.
  • A letter from any other county or state where you own a house, confirming no homestead is claimed there.
  • The divorce decree, if one applies.

Turning 62 by January 1 opens an added reduction on the school portion of assessed value, and approved exemptions step up again at ages 65, 68 and 70. The disability version asks for two doctors' letters, or one doctor's letter with a Social Security award letter, describing 100% disability. A married couple gets only one homestead.

sections.h2: If you think your value is wrong
sections.html:
Count 45 days from the mailing date on the notice. The Tax Assessor menu on the county site includes Notice of Assessment, Property Appeals, an appeal FAQ and conservation use rules, and the state's uniform PT-311A form asks you to commit to a route.

  • Board of Equalization: the route for value, uniformity, taxability or exemption fights. Henry lists this board under the Clerk of Superior Court, with its own members, forms, calendar, FAQ and appeal process pages.
  • Hearing officer: available only when non-homestead real estate exceeds $500,000.
  • Arbitration: restricted to value, and it needs a certified appraisal 45 days after the county acknowledges the appeal.

A superior court appeal follows written notice given within 30 days of the decision, after last year's tax is paid. Under O.C.G.A. 48-5-311, a final value of 85 percent or less of the board's figure entitles the owner to litigation costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

The commissioner runs judicial in rem tax sales at 140 Henry Parkway on the first Tuesday of the month at 10:00 AM. Once a sale happens, a twelve-month redemption period opens for interested parties, who repay the buyer's bid plus later taxes, assessments and a 20% premium. Before a sale, paying the tax along with fees, penalties and interest releases the lien.

If you are selling with a lien open, ask the closing agent for a payoff figure well ahead of time. Other levies are separate from the county bill, so ask the commissioner what else appears on yours.

A cash sale can close fast, but the lien still has to be cleared at the table. Call (770) 288-8180 early so the figure is ready.

faqs.q: When are Henry County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 16, with bills mailed by mid-September to the January 1 owner. The state default is December 20, so trust the date on your own bill.

faqs.q: How do I keep a Henry County lien off my name after selling?
faqs.a: Email page one of the settlement statement to propertytax@henrycountyga.gov inside the 90-day window. Without it the office records a lien against the January 1 owner.

faqs.q: How steep are Henry County late penalties?
faqs.a: Interest builds monthly, and 5% more is added every 120 days until penalties hit 20%. Make sure a mailed check has a USPS postmark before the deadline.

faqs.q: Where can I check a Henry County parcel's value?
faqs.a: Use the records search in the Tax Assessor section of the county website, or call (770) 288-7999, option 1. Billing questions go to the Tax Commissioner at (770) 288-8180.

faqs.q: Can I appeal in Henry County while my house is listed?
faqs.a: Yes. Listing does not pause or cancel the 45-day window. A lower final value also shrinks the bill that is divided at closing.
